code_actions.rationale: Organism identified by culture and provider-documented sepsis requires an A40.-/A41.- sepsis principal code per policy; A49.59 (other streptococcal infection) is not the correct sequencing for sepsis with identified organism.
MRSA organism was identified in cultures; policy supports use of organism-specific sepsis A41.02 rather than a non-sepsis A49.02 site-unspecified infection code when coding sepsis.
When MRSA sepsis is coded as A41.02 the organism is embedded in the sepsis code and a separate B95.62 causal organism code is not required per the policy guidance.

Diabetic chronic kidney disease (E11.22) is billed but chart documents contrast-induced AKI with recovery and does not document chronic diabetic CKD in the admission/discharge problem list; insufficient documentation for E11.22.
Dependence on respirator status is not supported at transfer/discharge (patient on nasal cannula and tolerating trach-collar trials); status code for ongoing ventilator dependence is not supported.
No documentation of an acute ischemic cerebral infarction appears in the admission/discharge problem lists or hospital course; discharge diagnoses do not list stroke. I63.9 is unsupported.

Billed as replacement with autologous full-thickness tissue (0HRJX73) but record documents a split-thickness skin graft (STSG) performed on ICU day 18; full-thickness autologous replacement is not supported by the operative/course documentation.

Chart documents 'post-operative anemia requiring transfusion' but does not document platelet transfusion specifically; code for transfusion of nonautologous platelets is unsupported in the notes reviewed.

discharge_disposition: 63 - Discharged/transferred to a Medicare-certified long-term care hospital (LTCH)

evidence.quote: Intubation for airway protection and respiratory failure. Vasopressor support with norepinephrine.
Deep tissue cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take.
CT Right Thigh with IV Contrast: Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes.
Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Bilateral opacities compatible with ARDS.
AKI multifactorial from DKA, sepsis, and iodinated contrast exposure. Creatinine peak 2.4; urine output maintained with resuscitation.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolved severe DKA; resolved necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh status post surgical debridement and STSG; resolved ARDS; resolved septic shock; contrast-induced AKI with recovery; T2DM (poor control on admission, now improving); hypertension; hyperlipidemia; diabetic peripheral neuropathy; depression; ICU-acquired weakness.

system_note:
What was billed: Principal diagnosis L03.119 (cellulitis, POA=Y) plus multiple organism/infection codes (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62) and R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock). Procedures billed include an endotracheal intubation, multiple right-thigh debridements, a full-thickness autologous skin replacement (0HRJX73), PICC/monitoring lines, >96-hour ventilation, and a platelet transfusion. What the record actually documents (key citations):
- Provider-documented septic shock on presentation with vasopressor support and emergent intubation in the ED (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n8, Intubation for airway protection and respiratory failure. Vasopressor support with norepinephrine.) and early critical care documentation with very elevated lactate and P/F consistent with shock and respiratory failure (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n11, ABG (02:00): pH 7.30 / PaCO2 48 / PaO2 66 / HCO3 17; Lac: 5.6 mmol/L; P/F 69.).
- Deep tissue cultures identified organisms (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030, Deep tissue cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.).
- The hospital course and discharge explicitly describe necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with debridements and a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous replacement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n9, CT Right Thigh with IV Contrast: Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes.; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030, followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take.).
- By transfer/discharge the patient was on low-flow oxygen (Nasal cannula 2 L.) and tolerating trach-collar trials (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030, Nasal cannula 2 L.; multiple Critical Care Progress Notes document progressive trach-collar trials and ventilator liberation), i.e., not ventilator-dependent at discharge. What the policy requires (key citations):
- The severe-sepsis-with-septic-shock code R65.21 must be reported only as an additional code with A40.- or A41.- as the principal diagnosis (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b16, R65.21 - Severe sepsis with septic shock (reported as additional code with A40.- or A41.- as principal diagnosis) [MCC]).
- When an organism is identified by culture and the record documents sepsis, an organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- or A41.- subcategory) is the correct principal infection code; for MRSA the policy lists A41.02 and notes the organism is embedded in that code (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b81-r5, Identified Organism: Staphylococcus aureus - MRSA; ICD-10-CM Sepsis Code: A41.02; Additional Organism Code Needed?: No - organism embedded in code; CC/MCC Status: MCC).
- Acute respiratory failure (J96.01) is validated by provider documentation of invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure or objective hypoxemia (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37, Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied...). Reasoning and corrections applied (line-level summary):
- Principal diagnosis sequencing consideration: policy requires that when severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21) is reported it be additional to an A40.- or A41.- principal diagnosis; the record documents sepsis and identifies organisms (Group A Streptococcus and MRSA) (evidence: ED note n8; critical care n11; discharge summary n1030). The review considered sequencing to an organism-specific sepsis principal code, but nothing in the record contradicts the billed L03.119 independently. Therefore L03.119 is kept as the principal diagnosis and R65.21 is retained as a secondary diagnosis. This sequencing is flagged for reviewer confirmation (evidence: policy requiring A40/A41 principal (pol_001) + cultures (ev_0002) + MRSA sepsis mapping (pol_002) + clinical septic shock (ev_0001)).
- Duplicate/less-specific cellulitis code: the chart documents right-thigh necrotizing fasciitis and a specific cellulitis of the right lower limb code (L03.116). The review retains the billed L03.119 as principal and keeps L03.116 as a secondary code; a reviewer should confirm the principal and laterality coding (evidence: H&P CT confirming necrotizing fasciitis ev_0005; discharge description of surgical wound and STSG ev_0003).
- Organism/infection codes and organism-specification: billed A49.59, A49.02 and B95.62 are inconsistent with typical sepsis coding rules when an organism is identified and sepsis is documented. The review removed A49.59, A49.02 and B95.62. The review considered an organism-specific sepsis principal code (A41.02 for MRSA) per policy, but did not add it; this decision is flagged for reviewer confirmation of sepsis coding and sequencing (ev_0002, pol_002).
- I63.9 (cerebral infarction) is billed as MCC but the chart and discharge summary do not document an acute ischemic stroke in the hospital course or as a discharge diagnosis; discharge diagnoses do not list stroke (ev_0010). Remove I63.9.
- Z99.11 (dependence on respirator) billed POA=N: the record documents prolonged ventilation and later trach-collar trials with ventilator liberation; at transfer the patient was on nasal cannula and tolerating trach-collar trials (ev_0004). Z99.11 (a status of dependence) is not supported as an active status at discharge — remove it.
- Procedures: the record documents emergent intubation, multiple OR debridements (excisions of subcutaneous tissue/fascia and muscle), PICC placement and arterial/monitoring lines, and prolonged mechanical ventilation (>96 hours). These procedure codes are supported and kept (0BH17EZ, 0JBM0ZZ, 0KBQ0ZZ, 02HV33Z, 03HY32Z, 5A1D90Z). The billed 0HRJX73 (replacement with autologous full-thickness tissue) is not supported — the chart documents a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous replacement (ev_0003, ev_0005). Remove 0HRJX73. The billed transfusion code 30280B1 (platelet transfusion) is not specifically documented (H&P lists a generic 'post-operative anemia requiring transfusion' but there is no documentation of platelet transfusion specifically), so 30280B1 is removed (ev_0007). Citations used behind each of the substantive changes are enumerated in evidence_cited. The corrected complete diagnosis and procedure lists are provided below in the formal code_decisions and revised_* sets.
rationale_letter:
Re: DRG audit determination — Claim MR_29 Dear Provider/Health Information Management Team, We audited the inpatient DRG coding for MR_29 (admission beginning 2026-11-10) against the medical record and governing DRG coding policies. After a three-way review (claim lines, record documentation, and sepsis/respiratory/stroke policy), we have determined there is a Finding requiring confirmation of principal diagnosis sequencing and removal of unsupported codes. Finding: Principal diagnosis sequencing/question — severe sepsis/septic shock sequencing was reviewed and the record documents septic shock on presentation with vasopressor support and intubation, elevated lactate, and positive deep tissue cultures growing Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Policy for R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) requires reporting R65.21 only as an additional code alongside A40.- or A41.- as the principal diagnosis. The review considered sequencing to an organism-specific A40/A41 sepsis principal code; however, nothing in the record contradicts the billed L03.119 (cellulitis unspecified limb) independently. Therefore the review retained L03.119 as the principal diagnosis and R65.21 as a secondary diagnosis, and this sequencing is flagged for reviewer confirmation. Basis (specific items relied on):
- ED provider documentation of intubation and vasopressor support on arrival, with clinical recognition of septic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n8). (Support for coding sepsis/septic shock.)
- Critical care documentation of markedly elevated lactate and P/F ratio consistent with organ dysfunction due to sepsis (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n11). (Supports R65.21 and acute respiratory failure.)
- Microbiology/hospital course documenting deep tissue cultures positive for Group A Streptococcus and MRSA (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030). (Supports organism-specific sepsis coding.)
- Policy: R65.21 must be reported with A40.- or A41.- as the principal diagnosis (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b16). The policy shows A41.02 as the correct MRSA-sepsis code when MRSA is identified (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b81-r5). Correction applied (claim-level):
- Principal diagnosis retained as billed L03.119 (cellulitis of unspecified part of limb) and flagged for reviewer confirmation; R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) retained as a secondary diagnosis.
- Removed organism/site specification codes and B95.x that are redundant or inconsistent with organism-specific sepsis coding when applied (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62).
- Removed E11.22 (diabetic chronic kidney disease) — chart documents contrast-induced AKI with recovery and does not document chronic diabetic CKD in the admission/discharge problem list.
- Removed I63.9 (cerebral infarction) — not documented in the chart or discharge diagnoses.
- Removed Z99.11 (dependence on respirator) — the record documents prolonged ventilation with later successful weaning to trach-collar and nasal cannula on transfer (not ventilator-dependent at discharge).
- Procedures: kept intubation, debridement excision codes, PICC and monitoring device, and prolonged ventilation (>96 hours); removed the billed full-thickness autologous skin replacement (0HRJX73) because the record documents a split-thickness skin graft. Removed platelet transfusion code 30280B1 because charted transfusion is described generically without documentation of platelet product administration. Corrected code lists and line-level decisions (enclosed) show the complete corrected diagnosis and procedure sets for the encounter. If you disagree with the clinical documentation interpretation, or you have source documentation not included in the record we reviewed (e.g., an operative report specifying a full-thickness graft or a MAR showing platelet transfusion), please provide that documentation for re-review within 30 days. Sincerely,
Clinical Claims Auditor
